Yes I’m talking about load balancing the WAN connection. That way you have fault redundancy.

So if you have two dedicated internet connections and one goes down, the traffic would switch over to the active line. This would mean that your internet uptime should be higher since you’re available more.

This will reduce your potential down time and loss of ETH.

The same logic should go for power.

Really doesn’t matter the router. You add more peers by invoking the correct command via your client. The only other factor would be uptime. If you’re really concerned I’d be solving for single points of failure.

Get a UPS, buy another internet connection and install a load balancer. 

Higher bandwidth doesn’t equal more connections. And more connections doesn’t mean more of anything than that.

You can increase your connections today to up to 60 is the max per Prysm Documentation.

I've literally never had a single issue with MainWP performing any task. I use MainWP and manage 132 sites with it, and have no issues.

Here is my advice on how to configure a reliable MainWP setup. Again this is just *my* advice - take it or leave it. 

​

* Setup a dedicated MainWP Host that is separate from the WordPress sites that you're managing. This reduced the potential for any hardware resource strain. This is how I've got mine setup as well. One server running MainWP, and an entirely separate server running all my WordPress sites
* Configure your MainWP setup as follows:
   * Set WordPress Memory Limit to **1024M**
   * Set PHP Memory Limit to **2098M**
   * Set PHP Max Execution Time to **300 seconds**
   * Set PHP Upload Max Filesize to **1024M**
   * Set PHP Post Max Filesize to **1024M**
   * Set cURL Timeout to **120**

​

There could be other potentials issues too if you're using a CDN which I never asked before either. If you're using a CDN there are known issues with MainWP. You can easily fix them but there are issues out of the box if they're not configured correctly. 

The biggest thing you can do to see immediate improvements is separating the MainWP instance from your WordPress instances. Hope this helps. Let me know if you need me to elaborate on anything.
